nodes.question: What percentage increase in emissions did the City of Portland experience after implementing a consumption-based inventory?
nodes.answer: The City of Portland saw a 118% increase in emissions after conducting a consumption-based inventory.
nodes.paragraph: While tracking emissions by sector appears as a simple accounting exercise, the practice can be complicated by consumption-based accounting. Emissions are most often reported on a per sector basis, but such sector-based emissions inventories lack a comprehensive view of a city S true metabolism (C40 2018 ). C40 Cities recommends consumption-based inventories, which also include emissions from all goods and services produced and con- sumed within a city (C40 2018). Such accounting can greatly increase reported emissions. For instance, the City of Portland saw a 118% increase in emissions after conducting a consumption-based inventory (City of Portland and Multnomah County 2015 ). Consider - ing such drastic increases when cities utilize a consumption-based emissions inventory, the 1 5% of municipal facilities share of local emissions would shrink even further as a true contribution to its community S total emissions. Upon the completion of a GHG inventory, cities develop mitigation and adaptation strategies for meeting emissions reduction targets and responding to future climate impacts (Boswell et al. 2010 ; Alloisio and Borghesi 2020 ). In the U.S., cities have primarily focused their actions on mitigating climate change.
